features.name: Custody anchor after the audit's fixes
features.description:
Custody anchor after the audit's fixes - feature F-1 of workplan ship-cost-reduction.
Make a ship start from the commit the audit actually finished on, not the one it first audited. Today `/audit-build` writes `- Audited commit:` into its report header before it chains `/implement-trd` in its chained reconcile mode (which edits code and runs a whole-branch review); that commit becomes `closed.json` `audit.auditedCommit`, and `custody.js reconcile` takes it as the anchor when none is set, so the first custody check of every ship finds changed code and re-proves (`packages/core/commands/audit-build.md` lines 251 and 307-325; `packages/core/lib/custody.js` `reconcile`). Change the close so the anchor custody reads is the branch head after the chained fix run has committed, and only when that fix run ended without a STUCK return and the re-audit (if any) passed; keep the report's audited commit as a separate, truthful field. A feature closed with no chained fix keeps today's behaviour. Cover it with Jest tests in `packages/core/lib/custody.test.js` and the audit-build contract tests.
Acceptance: `npx jest packages/core/lib/custody.test.js packages/core/commands` passes, including a new test where `closed.json` carries an audited commit followed by fix-run commits and `custody.js reconcile` sets the anchor at the post-fix head and returns `action: none` (no re-proof) on the next check.
Builds on: none.

features.name: Re-prove only what a change can affect
features.description:
Re-prove only what a change can affect - feature F-2 of workplan ship-cost-reduction.
Make custody's re-proof decision depend on the kind of change, building on 4.17.4's #101 (a merge-up already re-proves only criteria whose recorded files changed; `packages/core/lib/custody.js` header "BASE EXCUSE" and `affectedIds`). Four parts. (a) Every success criterion records the files it covers, not only `[LIVE]` tasks through `live-evidence.js` covers records: record covers for every criterion when it is proven (from the proving task's grounding Touches, falling back to the TRD task's file list), so the "no covers record re-proves on any shipped change" fallback in `affectedIds` stops applying to nearly everything; keep the fallback for a criterion that truly has no record. (b) Add `docs`, `deps` (dependency manifests and lockfiles) and `ci-config` (CI workflow files) change classes to `classifyPath` beside `ignored`, `test-only` and `shipped`. (c) Treat `OWNER-CALLS.md` as a record file in `packages/core/lib/record-files.js` `isRecordFile`, which stays the one definition. (d) Make the tier rules a per-product setting in `.claude/settings.json` under `ensemble.*` (the pattern `ensemble.docsAudit.thresholds` uses), with defaults from the strategy report's tier table: record files, docs only or a formatter commit re-prove nothing; test files or CI config only are left to CI; a dependency or lockfile change is left to CI unless the package is on an owner-named list (empty by default); a shipped change re-proves only the criteria whose covered files changed. An invalid setting stops with a reason naming it; an absent one uses the defaults. `scaffold-project.sh` must not overwrite an owner's value on refresh.
Acceptance: `npx jest packages/core/lib/custody.test.js packages/core/lib/record-files.test.js packages/core/lib/live-evidence.test.js` passes with new cases: a docs-only change, a lockfile change, a CI-workflow change and an `OWNER-CALLS.md` change each return no re-proof under the defaults; a shipped change re-proves only criteria whose covers include it; a setting override changes the outcome; an invalid setting is refused. `bats` for any `scaffold-project.sh` change.
Builds on: none.
Related: Custody anchor after the audit's fixes: touches the same custody and ship files; land after it where possible to avoid conflicts.

features.name: One retry for a re-proof
features.description:
One retry for a re-proof - feature F-3 of workplan ship-cost-reduction.
A re-proof (`/verify-build` in its chained criteria-subset mode, called by the custody gate in `packages/core/contracts/ship-custody-gate.md`) runs with `cap: 1` and no Debug stage (`packages/core/commands/verify-build.md`, the criteria-subset section), so one unmet or flaky criterion ends the ship STUCK (10 of 28 Storybook re-proof runs). Give it exactly one retry: when the first iteration leaves criteria unmet, re-run only those criteria once more, with no code edit, and take the second result. A criterion met on the retry is recorded as met with a `retried` flag (so a flake is visible, not hidden); one still unmet ends as today. No Debug pass inside a ship: it would edit code outside the recorded path and need its own review and re-proof. Keep the subset paths under `.trd-state/<feature>/reverify/` and the existing RETURN line.
Acceptance: `npx jest packages/core/commands/verify-build-criteria.test.js packages/core/contracts` passes with a case asserting the criteria-subset section of `verify-build.md` specifies one retry of only the unmet criteria and the `retried` flag; plus a unit test of whatever library computes the retry set.
Builds on: none.
Decisions: retry or debug pass: one re-run of the unmet criteria, no debug pass (owner's call, default taken unattended, 2026-11-11).

features.name: A CI fix sized to the failure
features.description:
A CI fix sized to the failure - feature F-4 of workplan ship-cost-reduction.
In `fix-findings` (`packages/core/contracts/ship-primitive-fix-findings.md` step 3), every non-lint row goes through `/implement-trd` in its chained shipping reconcile mode, with gate agents, the full battery and a whole-branch `/code-review` that applies its fixes, even for a one-line test fix; the review's edits then trigger another re-proof. Size the fix to the failure: classify each blocking CI row by the files the failure points at (the same classes custody uses: test-only, CI config, docs, product code). A failure whose fix lies only in test files or CI config is fixed directly, the affected tests or the workflow lint are run, the change is committed by pathspec, and no whole-branch review runs. A failure that needs a product-code change keeps today's reconcile path. A row the classification cannot place takes today's path. Sweep work (no TRD) keeps step 4 unchanged.
Acceptance: `npx jest packages/core/contracts/ship-primitives.test.js` passes with cases asserting the fix-findings contract routes a test-only and a CI-config row to the direct path (no `implement-trd`, no `/code-review`) and a product-code row to the reconcile path; plus a unit test for the row classifier if one is added.
Builds on: none.

features.name: Fewer STUCK endings in a ship run
features.description:
Fewer STUCK endings in a ship run - feature F-5 of workplan ship-cost-reduction.
Every stop in `/ship-build` ends STUCK, then a Forge escalation and a new session (57 ship-stage escalations in 14 days for Storybook). Let the run wait and loop where the next step is mechanical. The named case: inside the merge step (`packages/core/contracts/ship-primitive-merge.md` lines 53-55), CI failing on the new head after a merge-up is a `stop`; instead route it through the same fix-findings and wait-ci loop the `repeat` uses, bounded by a new `rounds=` parameter on `merge` (it has only `method=` today) defaulting to 2, the `repeat` default (`DEFAULT_ROUNDS` in `packages/core/lib/ship-sequencer.js`), and stop only when that bound is spent. Then go through the merge contract's "One rule for every stop" list and the sequencer's `stuck` paths (`packages/core/lib/ship-sequencer.js`) and, for each, decide whether it is a wait (a later check can clear it with no decision: CI still running, GitHub mergeability `UNKNOWN`), a bounded loop, or a real stop that needs a person; convert the first two and keep the third. Never bypass protection or merge without the custody proof. List each stop and its new classification in the TRD.
Acceptance: `npx jest packages/core/lib/ship-sequencer.test.js packages/core/contracts packages/core/lib/ship-build.seam.test.js` passes with a case where a red head after a merge-up loops through fix-findings and wait-ci and merges green within the bound, and one where the bound is spent and the run stops.
Builds on: A CI fix sized to the failure.

features.name: Re-proof results in the ship record
features.description:
Re-proof results in the ship record - feature F-6 of workplan ship-cost-reduction.
Forge plans a per-PR ship record and reads the ship block of `shipped.json`; Ensemble records nothing about re-proofs there today (`packages/core/lib/ship-sequencer.js`). Add a `reproof` block to the ship record: the number of re-proof runs, and for each run the criteria named, the criteria met (with the retry flag from the re-proof retry), the outcome string the run returned, the custody action and change classes that triggered it, and the time it took. The custody gate (`packages/core/contracts/ship-custody-gate.md`) writes each run through the sequencer, never by hand-editing `shipped.json`. Document the fields in the ship-build guide (`docs/guides/ship-build.md`) so Forge can read them.
Acceptance: `npx jest packages/core/lib/ship-sequencer.test.js` passes with a case that records two re-proof runs and reads them back from `shipped.json` with the fields above; the guide names each field.
Builds on: One retry for a re-proof.
